full_judgment:
Mr. Mirza Hussain Haider, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 06.12.2009, passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2437 of 2008, making Rule absolute, reversing the judgment and decree dated 20.06.2008, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No.63 of 2007 affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.03.2007, passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge in Title Suit No.287 of 2006, dismissing the suit.

2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal in short are:

That land measuring 1.29 acres in plot No.21, appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.70 (Umo) originally belonged to Yeasin Hazi who after transferring some part of it owned and possessed 0.29 acre of land. Thereafter he died leaving behind Dubuninnessa (Saburan Nessa) as his heir. Duburunnessa owned and possessed the said quantum of land till she transferred the same in favour of Khodeza Begum by a registered deed of lease bearing No.7752 on 15.12.1955 and delivered possession thereof to her and thereafter on 24.01.1956, Duburunnessa transferred her rent receiving interest to Khodeza Begum by registered deed of sale No.1142 dated 24.01.1956. Consequently S.A. record was prepared in the name of Khodeza Begum and she used to pay rents to the Government regularly. Khodeza Begum died leaving behind two sons and a daughter and they also used to own and possess the same like their predecessor. On 31.03.1969, the said heirs of Khodeza Begum transferred their entire share in the said 0.29 acre of land by registered deed of sale No.2269 dated 31.03.1969 in favour of Zumuruddin. Thereafter Zumuruddin got his name mutated in place of his predecessor and enjoyed the same till his death. At the time of his death he left behind two sons, four daughters and one wife (plaintiffs No.1 to 7), who have been possessing the entire suit land for more than 60 years, continuously, within the knowledge of the defendants and others.

On 19.09.2002, when the plaintiff No.1 went to the Tahsil Office to pay rent, the Tahsilder informed him that the suit land was recorded in the name of Bangladesh Railway and the Ministry of Defence. But actually neither of them had/have any title to and possession in the suit land. The cause of instituting the suit arose on 18.09.2002. Hence the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.287 of 2006.

3. Defendant Nos.1-3 (Divisional Estate Officer, Deputy Commissioner (Land and Building), Bangladesh Railway and Station Master, Narayangonj Rail Station) in one set and defendant No.4 (Government of Bangladesh through Deputy Commissioner, Narayangonj) in another set entered appearance and contested the suit by filing two separate written statements contending, inter alia, that the suit, as framed, is not maintainable and is barred by limitation. The specific case of defendant Nos.1-3, in short, is that long before, in 1882, 0.66 acre of land from the suit plot which was a ditch in nature, along with other lands was acquired for establishment of Dhaka-Mymenshing Rail Line. The same being a ditch it was leased out to one Monir Hossain for fish cultivation. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land.

4. The written statement of defendant No.4 supported the case of defendant Nos.1-3.

5. The trial Court dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 29.03.2007 upon hearing the parties on contest against which the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No.63 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Narayangonj, who transferred the same to the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Narayangonj, for disposal. The learned Additional District Judge upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record dismissed the appeal, affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, by his judgment and decree dated 29.06.2008.

6. Challenging the said judgment and decree passed by the Court of appeal below, the plaintiff-respondents filed Civil Revision No.2437 of 2008 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record, made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 06.12.2009 upon setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the Court below.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the defendant-appellants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1741 of 2010 before this Division and obtained leave giving rise to the instant civil appeal.

8. Mr. Shaheed Alam, learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that the suit land was validly acquired for Railway in L.A. Declaration in 1882 for setting up Narayangonj-Mymenshing Rail Line and accordingly RS. Record has been prepared in the name of the Railway and as such no question of title and possession of the plaintiffs arise. He submits that the High Court Division erroneously made the Rule absolute without reversing the concurrent findings of the Courts below. He further submits that the R.S. Khatian was prepared upon holding physical survey in the field and the plaintiffs having not been found in physical possession in the suit plot and the same being situated at the heart of Narayangonj town/city and no objection having been filed under Rules 30 and 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1954 the plaintiffs' claim of title and possession, since in purchase in 1969, is nothing but a got up story rather a cock and bull story which both the Courts below categorically found to be without any legal basis. Hence, according to him, the High Court Division committed error of law in setting aside the concurrent findings of the Courts below. He lastly submits that the High Court Division illegally interfered with the concurrent findings of fact of the Courts below that `Duburunnessa failed to prove her title on the basis of "Mourashi Patta" from C.S. recorded owner Yasin Hazi' and as such when Duburunnessa's title is not proved all subsequent transfers from Duburunnessa is nullity and as such void. Hence he prayed for allowing the appeal.

9. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Counsel with Mr. Nurul Amin, learned Senior Counsel, appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that although the defendants filed written statement, they did not specifically deny any of the specific assertions made in the plaint regarding the plaintiffs' ownership in the suit land which they purchased from subsequent transferees of Yeasin Haji. In the absence of such specific denial the assertion made by the plaintiffs is to be deemed as admission under Order VIII Rules 3 and 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that the plaintiffs produced all original deeds of 1955, 1956 and of 1969 and those being more than 30 years old documents those are very much genuine and admissible under Section 90 of the Evidence Act. Moreover these documents having not been challenged by the defendants those are admitted as genuine. He further submits that mere recording of any one's name in the R.S. record of right is not an evidence of title and as such the defendants having not proved the foundation of RS record of right, title does not vest in them and both the Courts below having concurrently found that the defendants failed to prove the foundation of the R.S. record, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute and decreed the suit. It is also submitted that the plaintiffs and defendants examined 2 witnesses each and the plaintiffs produced large number of documents but the Courts below without discussing single evidence dismissed the suit in violation of the mandatory provision of law. He further submits that the defendants never challenged the title of Duburunnessa Begum. Their only grievance is that the lease deed dated 15.12.1955 is hit by Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but the Courts below upon dismissing the facts and circumstances of the case and the law concurrently found that the said provision is not attracted in the present suit and as such the dismissal of the suit by the Courts below was illegal. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that the Court of appeal below misread and misconstrued the material evidence on record and without proper application of the same in its true perspective, made out a third case that the plaintiffs by making some documents have been trying to validate their title through the intervention of the Court as the Railway and the Defence Ministry had an indifferent attitude. Thus it committed serious error of law, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. But the High Court Division upon considering the law and the fact in its true perspective lightly found title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and accordingly made the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree of both the Courts below. Hence there being no illegality in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division the same does not call for any interference by this Division.

10. Considering the above facts and circumstances and the submissions made by the parties leave was granted to consider whether the suit land was validly acquired for Railway in LA Declaration of 1882; whether the R.S. record was rightly prepared in the name of Railway on actual field survey; whether the plaintiffs have title and possession on the suit land; whether the plaintiffs have been able to prove their possession in the suit land since their purchase in 1969 and whether the High Court Division was wrong in interfering with the concurrent finding that Duburunnessa failed to prove her title on the basis of "Mirashi Title" from the C.S. recorded owner Yeasin Hazi.

11. Admittedly both the Courts below found that the plaintiff's failed to prove the "Mirashi Title" of Duburunnessa, who transferred the suit land firstly, to Khodeza Begum and then from Khodeza, Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, purchased the suit land.

12. Clear case of the plaintiffs is that the original owner Yeasin Hazi died leaving behind Duburunnessa as his only heir who transferred firstly, the possession of the suit land to Khodeza Begum by registered deeds No.7752 dated 15.12.1955 and then transferred her rent receiving interest vide registered deed No.1142 dated 24.01.1956 respectively and accordingly Khodeza's name was recorded in the S.A. khatian. Thereafter the heirs of Khodeza Begum transferred the same to Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, by registered deed of sale No.2269 dated 31.03.1969 (28.03.1969) and Zumuruddin got his name mutated in the government record and then the plaintiffs, the heirs of Zumuruddin, are thus possessing the same within the knowledge of everyone for more than 60 years uninterruptedly and continuously having mutated their names vide Mutation Case No.5099/92-93 dated 19.04.1993 and 1503/93-93 dated 30.09.1993.

13. On the other hand, the defendants claim that the suit land is a ditch which was acquired in LA Declaration of 1882 for Narayangong-Mymenshing Railway Line and R.S. record has been prepared in the name of the Railway. It is further claimed that the suit land being a ditch the same was leased out to one Monir Hossain for five years for fish cultivation though the same has not been extended subsequently after 2005. Both the Courts below found that the plaintiffs failed to prove that Duburunnessa, the heir of Yeasin Hazi had "Mirashi Title". Side by side the Courts below also held that the defendant also failed to prove their-title in the suit land. On the other hand, in addition to the aforesaid finding of defendants' title the High Court Division, on perusal of the materials on record also held both the Courts below rightly found that Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not attracted in the present suit. The High Court Division also found that the defendants also did not produce any document to prove that the suit land was acquired by LA Declaration of 1882. On the question of possession the Courts below held that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their absolute possession on the suit land.

14. The High Court Division, upon scrutinizing the entire materials on record including the evidence of both PWs and DWs and the judgment of both the Courts below found that the defendants-failed to prove that the government acquired any title in the suit land, the defendants did not prefer any appeal or cross appeal against such finding and as such the concurrent finding of the Courts below remained unchallenged for which even if the plaintiffs' suit fails the defendants cannot claim any title over the suit land. Whereas in respect of the finding as to plaintiffs' title it appears that they have challenged the same in higher forums. So the defendants now cannot claim title in the suit land on the face of concurrent finding on the same against them specifically when the last Court of fact held the defendants failed to prove that the government has acquired any title in the suit land.

15. On perusal of the materials on record it appears that the Exhibits filed by the plaintiffs on the basis of which, two PWs clearly proved plaintiffs' title and possession in the suit land as they stated that the plaintiffs are cultivating fish in the suit land (ditch) and they are paying rents to the government regularly upon getting their names mutated vide two mutation cases mentioned above. PW2 specifically stated that he resides beside the suit land for last 15/20 years and all along he saw the plaintiffs, being the owners are possessing the same by cultivating fish. On the other hand, it appears that DW1 admitted that the suit land is a water body and it is a fallow land (পতিত জমি). On the other hand, DW2, the Litigant Inspector of Bangladesh Railway, deposed on behalf of the defendants No.1 to 3, that 'in 1882 the suit land along with other lands was acquired for setting up Narayangong-Mymenshing Railway Track. When the Railway Track was set up upon cutting the earth the suit land remained a ditch, a water body, which has been leased out to one Monir Hossain for five years. In his cross-examination he failed to say how much land Railway claims in the RS plot. He also could not say the name of the owner from whom the land was acquired nor could he say whether the C.S. and S.A. Khatians were prepared in the name of Railway. He also failed to say in whose name those were prepared. He categorically stated that he did not file any document to show that the land was ever acquired in 1882. He also admitted that he did not file any document to show that the suit land was acquired or leased out to Monir Hossain or anyone else. He admitted that after 5 years the lease has not been extended.

16. On consideration of the above evidence the High Court Division rightly found that the Courts below without discussing the evidence on record came to a wrong finding and thereby misdirected themselves in coming to the conclusion that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case of title and possession in the suit land.

<u>17. In respect of vesting of title upon Duburunnessa from her father, the CS recorded owner Yeasin Hazi, the High Court Division, upon discussing the entire facts and circumstances and the evidence on record, held that the assertion made in the plaint, in respect of devolution of title and possession on her and all subsequent transfers of title upon different transferees up to the plaintiffs' predecessor by different registered deeds and thereby recording their names in C.S. and S.A. record, the defendants having not denied either of those chronology of devolution of title and transfer in their pleadings or in their oral evidence the same, is treated as admission under Order VIII Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The law of pleadings is very clear in this respect. It is said that the defendant is found to deal specifically each allegation of fact, the truth of which is not admitted. The written statement must not only deal with specifically, the defendants must also answer the point of substance. If the denial of fact is not specific but evasive, the said fact shall be taken to be admitted. In such event, the admission itself being the proof, no other proof is necessary. This view is supported by a decision of this Division in the case of Zafela Begum Vs. Akitulla (16 BLC (AD) 46). The High Court Division, it further appears, took into consideration Exhibits 1, 1(Ka) and 1 (Ga) the Original deeds of transfer dated 17.12.1955, 21.1.01956 and 31.03.1969 which are all more than 30 years old documents, and as such are very much admissible in evidence under Section 90 of the Evidence Act and those documents have strong presumption of genuineness. But the defendants having not challenged either of those documents, their plea that the deed dated 17.12.1955 (Exhibit-1) is hit by Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not at all tenable. Thus the finding of all the Courts that 'Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not at all attracted in the present suit, is thus correct finding of fact and law.</u>

18. It further appears that the S.A. record was prepared in the name of Khodeza Begum who paid rents to the government and thereafter on transfer Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, got his name mutated in place of Khodeza Begum in the government record and lastly, the plaintiffs got their names mutated in place of their predecessor Zumuruddin in 1993 it is not understood as to how the R.S. record could be prepared in the name of the defendants after more than one hundred years of alleged acquisition in 1882 about which the plaintiffs came to know much later in 2002. In this respect, the High Court Division while reversing the finding of the Courts below considered Section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as well as several decisions of this Division and came to the conclusion that 'the burden of proof, in civil litigations initially is upon the plaintiff, but depending on the circumstances, it also shifts upon the defendant'. In the present case since the defendants did not deny the title of the plaintiffs, specifically, in their pleadings or in their evidences and since the defendants totally failed to prove acquisition of the suit land by LA Declaration of 1882 by adducing sufficient evidence, the burden of proof is thus shifted upon the defendants to prove their foundation of recording their names in the R.S. record. Having failed to do so the High Court Division, relying on the case of Cinmoy Chowdhury and another Vs. Sree Mridul Chowdhury and others (23 BLD (AD) 83) and Jonab Ali Mondal and others Vs. Md. Anowar Hossain and others (24 BLD 243), rightly came to the conclusion that the R.S. record has been prepared wrongly in the name of the defendants. Moreover, the defendants neither in their pleading nor in their depositions specifically denied publication of C.S. and S.A. record in the name of Yasin Hazi and his subsequent transferees through his daughter Duburunnessa. Apart from the above all the subsequent transferees got their names recorded and mutated in the government record and accordingly they had been paying rents to the government in respect of the suit land. A question may arise what is the presumptive value of final publication of record of rights. In the case of Akbor Ali Vs. Zahiruddin (30 DLR (SC) 81) it has been observed 'Even final publication of record of rights showing one in occupation of the suit land would not if so factor rebut the presumption raised by entries in the earlier record of rights. According to law both the records of rights shall be presumed to be correct at the respective dates of their final publication. Whether the presumption of correctness of the entries in the particular record of right has been rebutted or not shall have to be decided with reference to the facts and circumstances in each case. Thus the question as to whether the presumption of correctness of either of the record of right rebuttable on the other will depend upon the evidence adduced by the parties in the case.

19. In the present case it is claimed by the defendants that the suit land along with other lands was acquired by LA Declaration of 1882 but no evidence to that effect has been led by the defendants. On the other hand the plaintiffs claim that the Yasin Hazi, the original owner is a C.S. recorded tenant, which is generally known to have been prepared in 1920, i.e. much after the alleged acquisition of the suit land in 1882. Thereafter all the subsequent transferees, through Yasin Haji's daughter, Duburunnessa, which is not challenged by the defendants in their pleading or in the evidence, got their names recorded in S.A. record as well as got the same mutated in the government record. In the absence of specific assertions being not denied by the defendants specifically either in their written statement or in their evidence the Court is not inclined to permit the defendants to raise such a question at a belated stage nor the Court should consider such plea. Now question is on the face of all these records how the R.S. record could be prepared in the name of the defendants after more than one hundred years of so called acquisition. The evidence on records shows that the defendants miserably failed to prove such recording on any legal basis. Thus in the present case the plaintiffs having proved their better title, if not to the hilt, than that of the defendants it is enough to decide the case in their favours.

20. From the discussions made herein above since the plaintiffs have been successful in proving their genealogy of title and possession in the suit land and since the defendants failed to challenge the documents relied upon by the plaintiffs and also failed to prove their case of title and possession, it can clearly be held that the defendants have no title and possession in the suit land. On the other hand the plaintiffs could prove the title of Yeasin Hazi, the C.S. recorded tenant and thereafter devolution of title and possession upon his daughter Duburunnessa who in her turn transferred the same Khodeza Begum by two registered documents in 1955 and 1956 which are more than 30 years old documents and relying on such registered documents Khodeza Begum's name being recorded in the S.A. record and thereafter Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs having purchased the same got his name mutated in place of Khodeza Begum in the office of the Government, and after his death his heirs, the plaintiffs having got their names mutated, the title and possession of the plaintiffs are found to be proved.

21. Thus the High Court Division, in my considerate view, did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment upon setting aside the findings of the Courts below and decreeing the suit.

22. Accordingly we do not find any merit in this appeal. Hence this civil appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
